subject: Urgent: Aligning VP's 20-minute arrival window with our demo — BrightWorks
messages:
From: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@brightworks.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible shift for Wed's walkthrough — VP arrival window

Hi Kimberly,

Quick update from our side: our VP of Product will be landing later than planned on Wednesday — she has a 20‑minute window for the call starting ~11:40am PT and then needs to dash to an offsite. Given that, we want to avoid pulling her into a full 45 minute demo and instead give her the high‑value slice.

Can you advise whether we can:
- Compress the intro and product tour into 25 minutes and reserve the last 20 for the VP's live Q+A, or
- Shift the demo 30 minutes later so she can join for a fuller 20‑25 minute segment, or
- Proceed as scheduled and have one of your senior SEs cover the core 20 minutes with the VP dialling in only for the final handoff?

We don't want to cancel — just make sure her presence is impactful. We're happy to update the calendar once you confirm.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Collins
Head of Solutions — BrightWorks

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Possible shift for Wed's walkthrough — VP arrival window

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the heads up. All options are doable; I sketched two concrete proposals so we can lock the calendar quickly:

Option A (Compress + VP Q+A):
- 30 minute block total: 10 min rapid intro (value props + success metrics), 15 min focused demo on the integration flow, 5 min VP Q+A.
- We'll provide a one‑page condensed agenda and include two targeted screenshots.
- Pros: keeps current slot, minimal calendar churn.
- Cons: limits live exploration if VP wants deep technical follow‑ups.

Option B (Shift + Extended VP Window):
- Move meeting by +30 minutes; preserve 40 min: 20 min core demo, 15 min tailored use‑case discussion, 5 min wrap. VP joins for full 20 min.
- Pros: VP gets a meaningful block; room for follow ups.
- Cons: a calendar ripple for a few attendees.

Option C (SE-led core + VP cameo):
- Keep time. Marcus leads a 25 min technical walkthrough, then hand over to VP for a 15 min high‑level summary.
- Pros: preserves slot and depth.
- Cons: VP may miss some live nuance.

Attached: compact-demo-agenda.pdf and a one‑page mutual-action-plan CSV we can update post‑call. If you can confirm which option by EOD, we'll update invites and prep notes.

If helpful, Marcus can own the demo if we go with Option C — he can also prepare two short callouts for the VP to review quickly before joining.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
